title: Wafer-Level 1/f Noise Characterization of Scaled P-Type Nanosheets and Comparison with Planar HKMG Transistors
authors: Ruben Asanovski, Anabela Veloso, Ben Kaczer, Naoto Horiguchi, Jacopo Franco
abstract: We present a comprehensive wafer-level 1/f noise study of scaled Gate-All-Around (GAA) p-type nanosheet transistors and benchmark them against large-area planar High- \k{appa} Metal Gate (HKMG) devices to assess the impact of device architecture on reliability. By statistically analyzing noise data from 188 nanosheets, we extract the effective trap density in the dielectric and compare it to that of planar transistors with identical gate stack, comparable processing thermal budgets, and no specific reliability anneals. The effective trap density extracted from 1/f noise is comparable in planar and nanosheet architectures. This indicates that transitioning to GAA nanosheets does not increase noise, which remains governed by gate stack quality.
summary: This paper conducts a wafer-level study comparing 1/f noise in GAA nanosheet and planar HKMG transistors. By extracting the effective trap density from noise measurements, the authors demonstrate that the noise performance is governed by the gate stack quality, not the transition to the GAA nanosheet architecture. This suggests that gate stack optimization strategies applicable to planar devices will also benefit nanosheet transistors.
main_problem: To assess the impact of transitioning from planar High-kappa Metal Gate (HKMG) transistors to scaled Gate-All-Around (GAA) p-type nanosheet transistors on device reliability, specifically concerning 1/f noise.
main_result: The effective trap density extracted from 1/f noise is comparable between planar and nanosheet architectures, indicating that gate stack quality, not channel geometry, governs the noise response.
method: Wafer-level 1/f noise characterization and statistical analysis of transistor performance across multiple devices.
model_or_system: The study compares scaled p-type GAA nanosheet transistors against large-area planar HKMG pMOSFETs, using identical gate stacks and processing conditions for comparison.
key_observables: 1/f noise spectrum (S_vg), effective trap density (N_BT), Threshold voltage (V_T) and Subthreshold Swing (SS) CDFs.
important_parameters: Gate voltage overdrive (V_ov), operating temperature (25°C), and the comparison between planar and nanosheet geometries.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the noise behavior is primarily dictated by the quality of the gate stack dielectric, regardless of the channel architecture.
figures_summary: Figures compare the effective trap density (Fig. 11) and show consistent noise power spectral densities and device uniformity metrics between the two architectures.
paper_structure: The paper systematically characterizes the 1/f noise in both device types, extracts the effective trap density using established formulas, and then compares these quantitative results to argue that gate stack quality is the limiting factor for noise performance.
analysis_basis: full PDF text, analyzed in chunks
